column1: # Byte-parity anchors for scripts/differential.sh (issue #303 PR review).
# One committed path per line, sorted. The script requires the glob-discovered
# set to equal this file EXACTLY: a stray .sexp under fixtures/, examples/,
# bundles/ or corpus-units/ is a setup failure, not a free pass.
# Why a manifest and not a filename exclusion. The positive loop treats "both
# drivers exit 2 with empty stdout" as agreement, so any .sexp that is not a
# check-input@1 envelope decode-fails on both drivers and is counted as an
# agreeing anchor. Two such files existed (a map's map.core.sexp and
# map.verdict.sexp) and were excluded by name; the exclusion is correct for
# those two names and does nothing about the next file to arrive under a third
# name. The mutant half already pins itself against fixtures/mutants/MANIFEST.tsv
# for the same reason, and this is that discipline applied to the globbed half.
# Regenerate after adding or removing an anchor:
